case_identity.title: The Nannup Four
case_identity.summary: Four people — Simon Kadwill (real name Gary Felton/Simon Cook), his partner Chantelle McDougall, their 5-year-old daughter Leela, and friend Tony Popic — vanished from a farmhouse in a tiny town. Kadwill led a fringe doomsday belief system, used a stolen identity, and the group left behind dogs, clothes, and a partly eaten dinner. A coronial inquest left open whether it was cult murder-suicide or an engineered disappearance.

verified_facts.canonical_claim_en: From November 2003, Chantelle Jane McDougall, Gary Felton, also known as Simon Anthony Kadwill, and their daughter Leela McDougall lived on a rented rural property in Nannup; their friend Antonio Konstantin Popic resided with them intermittently in a caravan.

verified_facts.canonical_claim_en: Gary Felton was also known as Simon Anthony Kadwill and was described in the coronial finding as a British national and a self-styled spiritual leader.

verified_facts.canonical_claim_en: On 13 July 2007, Chantelle sold her car to a car dealer in Busselton and sold three of her dog's puppies to a pet shop there; on 14 July 2007, she sold the remaining puppy and the adult dogs to Carolyn French, who drove to Nannup to buy them.

verified_facts.canonical_claim_en: On 16 July 2007, the owners of the rural property found the house vacated in spotless condition, with several valuable furnishings left behind, and found a note from Chantelle indicating that the group had gone to Brazil.

verified_facts.canonical_claim_en: In October 2007, Chantelle's father reported to police in Victoria that Chantelle and Leela were missing and that he had serious concerns for their welfare; Tony's brother contacted Western Australian Police in early November 2007 to report Tony missing.

verified_facts.canonical_claim_en: On 31 October 2007, police attended a remote bush location near Northcliffe after prison workers reportedly found a woman's old red T-shirt and reported smelling dead flesh; police seized the T-shirt, but the coronial finding records no forensic examination of it and no recorded search of the bushland at that time.

source_refs.title: Coroners Act, 1996

verified_facts.canonical_claim_en: Police later could not locate the T-shirt seized near Northcliffe, and the coronial finding states that investigators did not follow up that and other reports during the original investigation, resulting in lost investigative opportunities.

source_refs.title: Coroners Act, 1996

verified_facts.canonical_claim_en: A full forensic examination was not conducted of the group's house and caravan after the missing-persons report; a later search in April 2008 also did not include a full forensic examination because time had passed and new tenants occupied the property.

verified_facts.canonical_claim_en: On 12 and 13 January 2015, a Western Australia Police dive squad searched the five dams on the property that had existed in 2007; the search revealed no evidence of the group.

verified_facts.canonical_claim_en: On 15 July 2007, Tony's mobile phone was used in Northbridge, a man identified as Tony received a pizza in King's Park, and a person using Tony's driver's licence checked into the Underground Backpackers Hostel; the coroner considered it highly likely that Tony had traveled to Perth that day.
verified_facts.speaker: Barry Paul King
